title: Prove intrinsic P104 translated-progress bound and audit canonical adapters
body:
This closes a specific hypothesis left by [PR #3954](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3954) and [PR #3962](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3962): how much persistent progress can a translated P104 call claim? For the unchanged intrinsic endpoints, matched Clifford translations have total progress at most **2312** under the role-local, common-chart grammar. The proof uses the actual native width `phi(M)=rank_F2(B)` and the conjugacy-invariant upper bound `rank(M-I)`; it does not assume that translation preserves the paid profile.

There is a source-bound qualification. At actual port X0 (`q=386`), the bare canonical endpoint has a legal matched Clifford translation that raises native width from **8 to 9**. Its old rank-zero intrinsic adapter then has width **2**; including that adapter restores the intrinsic width bound **8**. The 208 intrinsic monomial adapters are distinct from the later 208 rank-one side-correction transports. A whole canonical-word control reprices every one of the 1410 transports: mass **2248**, progress **2066**, excess **182**, compared with the original excess **56**. This is a transport-only control, not a complete corrected-call invoice.

The theorem is endpoint-dependent: if a verified changed word leaves all Y roles at F9, the corresponding sharp cap becomes **2416**. The package explicitly leaves the changed word's logical return, paid corrections, physical wrappers and global caller bill open. It does not import an unverified sibling saving, claim a universal P104 barrier, or change the selected frontier.

All changes are in `research/p104-translated-progress/`. Canonical main remains `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. The coordinated overlap pass covered all 676 open PR bodies including drafts at 07:38:11 UTC, with later targeted refreshes; the [scope claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3954#issuecomment-6262365386) distinguishes this endpoint/rank audit from the parallel correction, coding and changed-consumer work.

Validation on published head `c6ea4442a62975244ca74b320587d7a3fe791905`:

- Source-bound checks authenticate nine canonical inputs, reconstruct 14400 root pairings and 104 physical ports, and check all 280 endpoint cocycles and 1410 original native tariff uses.
- A separate checker imports neither the primary verifier nor the producer. It checks all 518400 Sp(4,2) products, 2160 matched translations, six exact Gaussian-rational operator actions, and the actual counterexample/adapter matrices.
- Six optimized test groups include seven actual CLI receipt/source mutations. Every mutation is preceded by a passing pristine private-fixture run, so rejection cannot be attributed to an already broken fixture.
- Registered package replay, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export check and all three optimized commands in a read-only Git-free export pass. The frozen export has 20 files including its receipt; their bytes and read-only modes remain unchanged.
- Export SHA256: `a3211c2cfeb54e86ab1328db964f5ada50d2c1f723991a7c6fa8915131700a70`.

Unsigned symplectic rank is not a phase certificate, a general scalar-operation lower bound, or all-size admission. Coupled operator-valued charts fall outside the proved potential. The next admissible experiment is a real changed endpoint or coupled interface with its full source-to-return accounting.

Credit: Rohan Arun/[PR #1972](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1972) and Adam Gall/[PR #1940](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1940) for the scalar/frame word; [PR #1991](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1991) prepared for Chafik Boukhalfa and its credited native compiler/physical-label predecessors, including icekylinx; Douglas Colkitt and the residual/caller notes; [PR #3882](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3882)/[PR #3894](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3894)/[PR #3940](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3940) for the correction/caller stream; [PR #3954](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3954)/[PR #3962](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3962) for the conditional gate; [PR #3961](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3961)/[PR #3965](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3965) for distinct boundary/lifetime obligations, and ToikY/[PR #3966](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3966) for phase-uniform gauges. Exact replay inputs, compiler notice and license remain pinned. Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex multi-agent assistance; no independent human or proof-assistant review claimed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-translated-progress`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39219896987) passes at this exact head: planning, focused package replay and committed-input preservation succeed.
